title: Advanced Combinatorics
relevance: Advanced counting formulas, Catalan numbers, derangements, and pigeonhole arguments show up often in coding OAs and quant-style SDE interviews.

phases.goal: Establish the core advanced counting formulas candidates must recall cold.

must_hit.point: Stars and bars: n identical objects into k distinct bins has binom(n+k-1, k-1) ways; if each bin gets at least one, it is binom(n-1, k-1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States both unrestricted and positive-integer forms with the correct binomial arguments.

must_hit.point: Inclusion-exclusion expands |A ∪ B ∪ …| by alternating sums of single, pairwise, triple, … intersections.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the alternating PIE expansion rather than only pairwise union.

must_hit.point: Hockey-stick identity: sum from i=k to n of binom(i,k) equals binom(n+1, k+1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recalls the closed form binom(n+1, k+1) for that binomial sum.

must_hit.point: Catalan number Cn equals (1/(n+1)) binom(2n, n) and counts balanced parentheses, triangulations, valid stack sequences, and non-crossing lattice paths.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the formula and names at least two of those Catalan objects.

must_hit.point: Derangements: Dn = n! times sum from k=0 to n of (-1)^k / k!; for large n, Dn is about n!/e.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the factorial-sum formula and the large-n n!/e approximation.

probes: State the stars-and-bars formulas for unrestricted and at-least-one distributions, and give the Catalan and derangement formulas.

hints.1: Think about how bars partition identical items, and about the closed forms for Catalan and derangements.
hints.2: Unrestricted stars and bars uses binom(n+k-1, k-1); Catalan is (1/(n+1)) binom(2n,n); derangements involve the alternating 1/k! series.
hints.3: Say: binom(n+k-1,k-1) or binom(n-1,k-1) if nonempty; PIE alternating intersections; hockey-stick to binom(n+1,k+1); Cn=(1/(n+1))binom(2n,n); Dn=n!∑(-1)^k/k! ≈ n!/e.

phases.goal: Show how to reduce constrained distributions, PIE complements, and labeled equal-size assignments to the right formula.

must_hit.point: Lower bounds are handled by pre-allocating the minimums, then applying unrestricted stars and bars to the remainder.
must_hit.evidence_hint: For example, allocates minima then counts free distribution of leftover identical units.

must_hit.point: An upper bound like x1 ≤ 4 is handled by unrestricted stars-and-bars total minus the cases that violate the bound.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Subtracts the pre-allocated excess cases from the unrestricted count.

must_hit.point: Distinct items into equal-size labeled groups use successive combinations (multinomial), not stars and bars.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Chooses groups sequentially, e.g. binom(6,2)×binom(4,2)×binom(2,2) for six distinct requests onto three servers two each.

must_hit.point: Surjective-function counts and 'must include letters' password counts use total maps minus PIE over missed codomain elements or required letters.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Starts from total functions or 26^5-style totals and applies PIE on missing images or missing required characters.

probes: How do you count allocations with lower bounds, with an upper bound on one variable, and equal loads of distinct requests onto distinct servers?

hints.1: Ask whether objects are identical or distinct, and whether constraints are floors, ceilings, or onto-ness.
hints.2: Pre-allocate minima; complement upper bounds; use multinomial for distinct equal groups; use PIE for onto or 'must contain' constraints.
hints.3: Walk an example: give minima then stars-and-bars on remainder; total minus x1≥threshold; binom choices for labeled equal piles; total^n minus PIE misses.

phases.goal: Distinguish when identical-item formulas, labeled multinomials, and unlabeled-group divisions apply.

must_hit.point: Stars and bars applies to identical objects in distinct bins; distinct objects need combinations or multinomial coefficients instead.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly refuses stars and bars when requests/items are distinct.

must_hit.point: Divide by k! only when the k groups are identical or unlabeled; do not divide when the bins or servers are distinct.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says labeled servers keep the multinomial product without a trailing /k!.

probes: When distributing items, when do you use stars and bars versus a multinomial, and when if ever do you divide by k!?

hints.1: The key fork is whether the items are identical and whether the groups are labeled.
hints.2: Identical→stars and bars; distinct equal labeled piles→product of binomials; /k! only for unlabeled groups.
hints.3: Candies to children: stars and bars; six distinct requests, two per distinct server: 15×6×1 with no /3!.

phases.goal: Apply Catalan, derangement, and pigeonhole patterns to classic interview settings.

must_hit.point: Grid paths that never go above y=x, balanced parentheses, valid stack sequences, and structurally unique BSTs are Catalan counts Cn.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recognizes those OA phrasings as thinly veiled Cn calculations.

must_hit.point: Probability of a full derangement is Dn/n!; for large n it approaches 1/e, and Dn obeys Dn = n Dn-1 + (-1)^n.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses Dn/n! and either the 1/e limit or the recurrence with known small Dn values.

must_hit.point: Pigeonhole proofs often hide the holes as odd parts, cumulative-sum offsets, or geometric cells such as quadrants of a square.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names odd-part bins, {ai} with {ai+offset}, or subdividing a region so two points share a cell.

probes: A problem asks for valid bracket strings, Secret Santa with no self-matches, or a closest-pair guarantee among points in a square—what counting tool do you reach for?

hints.1: Match the story to Catalan, derangements, or pigeonhole bins.
hints.2: Brackets/non-crossing/BST→Catalan; no fixed points→Dn or 1/e; existence of a close pair or divisor→pigeonhole.
hints.3: E.g. C5 for 5×5 diagonal-safe paths; D5/120 for five-person Secret Santa; four half-side squares force two of five points within diagonal √2/2.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Use stars and bars when objects are identical and bins are distinct; when objects are distinct and groups have prescribed sizes, use successive combinations (multinomial). Dividing by k! is only for unlabeled/identical groups, not for distinct servers or asset classes.
Exact answers use Dn = n!∑(-1)^k/k! or the recurrence Dn = n Dn-1 + (-1)^n; for large n (e.g. a 52-card matching), Dn/n! is practically 1/e.

gotchas.trap: Using k instead of k-1 when placing bars in stars and bars.
gotchas.correction: k distinct groups need only k-1 partitions/bars, so the binomial is binom(n+k-1, k-1) (or the positive form binom(n-1, k-1)).

gotchas.trap: Dividing a multinomial assignment by k! when the bins are distinct.
gotchas.correction: Only divide by k! for unlabeled groups; distinct servers keep the raw product of combinations.

gotchas.trap: Applying hockey-stick as if every sum starts at binom(k,k).
gotchas.correction: The identity always starts at binom(k,k); if the given sum starts higher, compute the full hockey-stick sum and subtract the missing early terms.

gotchas.trap: Treating 'exactly r fixed points' as choose-r times a free permutation of the rest.
gotchas.correction: The remaining items must themselves be a derangement; otherwise fixed points sneak back in.
